definition_zh: 命令；指挥；掌握；博得
definition_en: an official order, control over a group of people, or to order someone to do something
core_image: 军官抬手一声令下，整队人同时转身
scene: 队长举起手，所有人立刻停下脚步。The officer gave a command and the soldiers stood still.
sceneCN: 这里 command 指「命令」（第 1 个义项：上级下达的指令）；句意是军官下达命令，士兵们站定不动。

senses.title: An official order
senses.definition: an order given by someone with authority
senses.definitionCN: 有权者下达的指令
senses.example: The general gave the command to advance.
senses.exampleCN: 将军下达了前进的命令。
senses.why: The earliest sense in English is a direct order from a leader.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在英语里最早的义项就是首领直接下达的指令。

senses.title: Control over a group
senses.definition: the power to direct people or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 指挥人员或掌控局面的权力
senses.example: She was in command of the whole fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 她指挥着整支舰队。
senses.why: Whoever gives the orders holds the power, so order becomes control.
senses.whyCN: 下达命令的人掌握着权力，于是命令变成了掌控。

senses.title: To order or deserve
senses.definition: to order someone to do something, or to deserve and receive respect
senses.definitionCN: 命令某人做事，或赢得并得到尊敬
senses.example: Her calm voice commanded respect.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉静的声音赢得了尊敬。
senses.why: Authority both issues orders and draws respect without asking.
senses.whyCN: 权威既下达命令，也不必请求就赢得尊敬。

intro.en: Command comes from Latin mandare, to entrust, strengthened by the prefix com-.
intro.cn: command 来自拉丁语 mandare（托付），并由前缀 com- 加强语气。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand something over or entrust a task.
items.cn: mandare 意为把东西交出去或把任务托付给人。

items.en: Commandare added com- and took on the sense of ordering.
items.cn: commandare 加上 com-，带上了下令的意味。

items.en: Old French comander meant to order and to entrust.
items.cn: 古法语 comander 兼有下令与托付之意。

items.en: English command entered as both a noun and a verb of authority.
items.cn: 英语 command 以名词与动词两种身份进入，都表示权威。

items.en: It widened to mastery of a language and to earning respect.
items.cn: 它的用法扩展到语言的掌握与赢得尊敬。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in spelling to command, while the meaning group lists verbs of ordering and directing.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 command 拼写相近的词，近义组列出下令与指挥的动词。

entries.definition: to tell someone to do something
to control or manage an activity

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a voice giving an order, then move to the power behind it and to the respect it earns.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一声下令开始，再走到命令背后的权力与它赢得的敬意。

normal.en: Com- plus mandare, to entrust, means a task handed down with authority.
normal.cn: com- 加 mandare（托付），指带着权威交办下去的任务。

normal.en: The one in command is the one whose words end discussion.
normal.cn: 处于指挥位置的人，话一出口讨论就结束。

normal.en: A good command of English means the language obeys you.
normal.cn: 良好的英语运用能力，意味着这门语言听你调遣。

normal.en: Command respect is respect you never had to ask for.
normal.cn: 赢得尊敬，是你从不必开口索要的尊敬。

normal.en: Commander adds -er and becomes the person who commands.
normal.cn: commander 加 -er，就成了下命令的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand and a whole line turning at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，整排人同时转身。

abstract.en: Picture a map table lit by one lamp on a ship's bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象舰桥上被一盏灯照亮的地图桌。

abstract.en: Picture a room falling silent when one person begins to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人开口时，整个房间安静下来。

examples.en: The captain gave a short command and the crew moved.
examples.cn: 船长下达了简短命令，船员们行动起来。

examples.en: She has a good command of three languages.
examples.cn: 她精通三门语言。

examples.en: His honesty commanded the trust of everyone there.
examples.cn: 他的诚实赢得了在场每个人的信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 command 记成 com（一起）加 mand（手）：手一挥，所有人一起动，就是命令。

root: 源自拉丁语 mandare（托付），加前缀 com- 后成 commandare，本义是把任务交办下去，后引申为命令、指挥与掌握。

sensesIntro.en: From an order spoken aloud, to the power that backs it, and finally to the respect and mastery it brings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从说出口的命令，到支撑它的权力，再到它带来的敬意与掌握。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an officer raising a hand and a whole line turning as one.
core.cn: 核心意象：军官抬手一声令下，整队人同时转身。

branches.en: The spoken order is the sense that entered English first.
branches.cn: 说出口的命令是最早进入英语的义项。

branches.en: Control is what makes an order more than a request.
branches.cn: 正因为有掌控力，命令才不只是请求。

branches.en: The verb covers both ordering people and earning respect.
branches.cn: 动词义既包括对人下令，也包括赢得尊敬。

branches.en: An order and the power behind it are two views of one act.
branches.cn: 命令与它背后的权力，是同一动作的两个视角。

branches.en: Mastery of a language is control without a single shout.
branches.cn: 对一门语言的掌握，是一声不喊的掌控。

intro.en: Command is a free base that forms agent nouns with -er and abstract nouns with -ment.
intro.cn: command 是自由词基，用 -er 构成施动者名词，用 -ment 构成抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mandare, to entrust, is the root shared with mandate and demand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mandare（托付）是与 mandate、demand 共有的词根。

items.exampleCN: 这个系统接受语音指令。

items.exampleCN: 几位指挥官在基地会面。

definition_zh: 指挥官；司令；海军中校
definition_en: a person who is in charge of a group of soldiers or of a military operation
core_image: 站在队列最前方，肩上扛着全队责任的那个人
scene: 舰桥上，他对着地图下达最后的指令。The commander ordered his troops to hold the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 commander 指「指挥官」（第 1 个义项：部队的负责人）；句意是指挥官命令部队守住大桥。

senses.title: A military leader
senses.definition: an officer who leads soldiers or directs a military operation
senses.definitionCN: 率领士兵或指挥军事行动的军官
senses.example: The commander gave the order to withdraw.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥官下达了撤退的命令。
senses.why: The ending -er marks the person who does what the base verb names.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 标记出执行词基动作的那个人。

senses.title: A naval rank
senses.definition: a rank in the navy between lieutenant commander and captain
senses.definitionCN: 海军中位于少校与上校之间的军衔
senses.example: She was promoted to commander last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年春天晋升为海军中校。
senses.why: Navies turned the job title into a fixed rank with its own badge.
senses.whyCN: 海军把这个职务名称固定成一个有专属标识的军衔。

senses.title: Head of a police unit
senses.definition: the officer in charge of a police division in some countries
senses.definitionCN: 某些国家中负责一个警区的主管警官
senses.example: The commander briefed the press that morning.
senses.exampleCN: 那位警队主管当天上午向媒体作了通报。
senses.why: Any group that must be led borrows the military word for its head.
senses.whyCN: 任何需要被带领的队伍，都会借用军队里称呼首领的词。

intro.en: Commander is command plus -er, the ending for the person who performs an act.
intro.cn: commander 由 command 加 -er 构成，词尾表示执行动作的人。

items.en: Mandare meant to entrust a task to someone.
items.cn: mandare 意为把任务托付给某人。

items.en: Commandare carried the sense of giving orders.
items.cn: commandare 带上了下达命令的意思。

items.en: Old French comandeor named the one who gives orders.
items.cn: 古法语 comandeor 指下命令的那个人。

items.en: English commander first meant a leader of armed men.
items.cn: 英语 commander 最初指武装人员的首领。

items.en: It became a formal rank in armies and navies.
items.cn: 它在陆军与海军中成为正式军衔。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same command stem, while the meaning group names leaders of groups.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在同一 command 词干上的词，近义组列出带领队伍的各类首领。

a person who holds a position of command
a person who guides a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one person giving orders, then move to the rank and to police units that use the same title.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个人下命令开始，再走到军衔与沿用同一称呼的警队。

normal.en: Commander is command plus -er, so it is the person, not the order.
normal.cn: commander 是 command 加 -er，指人而不指命令。

normal.en: A commander in chief stands above every other commander.
normal.cn: 总司令站在所有其他指挥官之上。

normal.en: In the navy the word is a rank, not just a job.
normal.cn: 在海军里这个词是军衔，不只是职务。

normal.en: The plural commanders simply adds s.
normal.cn: 复数 commanders 只加一个 s。

normal.en: Wherever people must be led, someone takes the title.
normal.cn: 凡是有队伍需要带领的地方，就有人接过这个称呼。

abstract.cn: 想象一个身影站在舰桥上俯视地图。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers turning as one at a raised hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，一列士兵同时转身。

abstract.en: Picture a room of reporters waiting for one short statement.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子记者等着一段简短声明。

examples.en: The commander ordered his troops to hold the bridge.
examples.cn: 指挥官命令部队守住大桥。

examples.en: A good commander listens before giving orders.

examples.en: The commanders met to plan the next move.
examples.cn: 各位指挥官会面商定下一步行动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commander 记成 command（命令）加 er（人）：下命令的那个人，就是指挥官。

root: 由 command 加表人的后缀 -er 构成，词根上溯拉丁语 mandare（托付）与 commandare（下令），本义是下达命令的人。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who leads troops, to a fixed naval rank, and finally to the head of a police division.
sensesIntro.cn: 从带领部队的人，到固定的海军军衔，再到警区主管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the figure at the front of a line, carrying the whole group's responsibility.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在队列最前方，肩上扛着全队责任的那个人。

branches.en: Leading soldiers is the original and broadest sense.
branches.cn: 率领士兵是最初也最宽泛的义项。

branches.en: A navy turned the title into a rank with a badge.
branches.cn: 海军把这个称呼变成带标识的军衔。

branches.en: Police forces borrowed the word for a division head.
branches.cn: 警队借用这个词来称呼警区主管。

branches.en: The same word names a role and a grade at once.
branches.cn: 同一个词同时指职务与等级。

branches.en: Army and police share the idea of one person answerable for many.
branches.cn: 军队与警队共享一个观念：一人为众人负责。

intro.en: Commander is a derived agent noun, and its wider family comes from the base command.
intro.cn: commander 是派生的施动名词，更大的家族来自词基 command。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mandare, to entrust, links commander with mandate and demand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mandare（托付）把 commander 与 mandate、demand 连在一起。

items.exampleCN: 各位指挥官共用同一个无线电频道。

items.example: The commandant greeted the new recruits.

items.example: He pointed commandingly at the door.

definition_zh: 开始；着手；开始存在；（仪式）开始
definition_en: to begin, especially in a formal or official way
core_image: 推开一扇门，跨过门槛，让一件事正式起步
scene: 奠基仪式上，铁锹落下第一铲土。 The first spadeful of soil was turned, and the construction work commenced.
sceneCN: 这里 commence 是「正式开始」（第 2 个义项：仪式或工程按程序启动）；句意：第一铲土落下，工程正式开始了。

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Begin an activity
senses.definition: to begin doing something, especially something planned or formal
senses.definitionCN: 开始做某事，尤指有计划或正式的事
senses.example: The meeting will commence at nine sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 会议将于九点整开始。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind it means 'to go in, enter'. To commence is to step across a threshold into an activity that now counts as begun.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的拉丁动词意为“走入、进入”。commence 就是跨过一道门槛，进入一件从此算作“已开始”的事。

senses.title: Start a ceremony or formal event
senses.definition: of a ceremony, ceremony, or public event, to open in the prescribed way
senses.definitionCN: （典礼或公共活动）按既定程序开场
senses.example: The graduation ceremony commenced with the national anthem.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业典礼在国歌声中开始。
senses.why: Formal events have a marked entrance. Commence is the word for that moment when the ceremony leaves the waiting state and officially runs.
senses.whyCN: 正式活动有一个明确的“入场点”。commence 就指典礼离开等待状态、正式开始运转的那一刻。

senses.title: Take effect legally
senses.definition: of a contract, lease, or rule, to begin to have legal force
senses.definitionCN: （合同、租约或规则）开始具有法律效力
senses.example: The lease commences on the first of May.
senses.exampleCN: 租约自五月一日起生效。
senses.why: A contract also has a threshold: before a stated date it exists on paper but does nothing. Commencing is the moment it starts to bind the parties.
senses.whyCN: 合同也有一道门槛：在约定日期之前，它只在纸上存在，并不起作用。commence 就是它开始约束各方的时刻。

senses.title: Come into existence
senses.definition: of an era, process, or state, to begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: （时代、过程或状态）开始存在
senses.example: A new era of trade commenced after the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订后，贸易的新时代开始了。
senses.why: Here nothing is literally done by a person: a period opens. The verb describes the first point of a stretch of time rather than a first action.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不是某个人在做动作，而是一段时期打开了。动词描述的是时间段的第一个点，而不是第一个动作。

senses.title: Commence work or duty
senses.definition: to start work, duty, or a job, especially on a fixed date
senses.definitionCN: 开始工作、履职或上任，尤指在某个固定日期
senses.example: She commences duty as head nurse next Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 她下周一正式出任护士长。
senses.why: A post is a role someone enters. The word marks the crossing from appointee to office-holder, which is why it suits official appointments.
senses.whyCN: 职位是人“进入”的角色。这个词标记了从“被任命者”到“在职者”的跨越，因此适合正式任命。

senses.title: Commencement: the graduation ceremony
senses.definition: the noun commencement, in American English, the ceremony at which degrees are awarded
senses.definitionCN: 名词 commencement，在美式英语中指授予学位的毕业典礼
senses.example: Parents flew in for commencement.
senses.exampleCN: 父母专程飞来参加毕业典礼。
senses.why: The ceremony marks not the end of study but the beginning of the next stage. The noun keeps the verb's forward-facing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个典礼标记的不是学业的结束，而是下一阶段的开始。这个名词保留了动词“朝前看”的含义。

senses.title: Commence proceedings
senses.definition: to begin a legal action or official procedure
senses.definitionCN: 开始法律诉讼或正式程序
senses.example: The tenant commenced proceedings against the landlord.
senses.exampleCN: 租客对房东提起了诉讼。
senses.why: Legal procedure is a sequence with a formal first step. Commencing names that step, so the phrase is fixed in court language.
senses.whyCN: 法律程序是一套有正式第一步的序列。commence 命名了那一步，因此这个搭配在法庭语言里是固定的。

senses.title: Commencing: opening or initial
senses.definition: the present participle used attributively, meaning opening or initial
senses.definitionCN: 现在分词作定语，表示“开端的、起初的”
senses.example: The commencing chapter sets out the main argument.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇那一章提出了主要论点。
senses.why: The participle captures the first moment as it happens. Used before a noun, it labels whatever stands at the entrance of a sequence.
senses.whyCN: 现在分词捕捉正在发生的“第一刻”。放在名词前，它就标注处于序列入口的那个东西。

intro.en: Commence is a French-shaped verb built on a Latin beginning. The 'entering' image is visible in its Latin ancestors, and the graduation sense is an American development.
intro.cn: commence 是一个法语形的动词，建立在拉丁语“开始”之上。“进入”的意象在其拉丁语祖先里看得见，毕业典礼义则是美式英语的发展。

items.en: Initium meant 'a beginning', and inire meant 'to go in, enter, begin'. The physical image is stepping inside.
items.cn: initium 意为“开端”，inire 意为“走入、进入、开始”。其具体意象是“迈步进入”。

items.en: A reconstructed *cominitiare added com- 'together' as an intensifier to initiare 'to begin'. The com- does not mean 'with someone' here; it strengthens the start.
items.cn: 重构形式 *cominitiare 在 initiare“开始”前加了加强语气的 com-。这里的 com- 不是“与人一起”，而是强化“开始”这一动作。

items.en: Old French comencier, commencier (11c.) carried the word into everyday French with the sense 'to begin'.
items.cn: 古法语 comencier、commencier（11 世纪）把这个词带入日常法语，意为“开始”。

items.en: English took commence from French in the 14th century. It has always sounded more formal than begin, which is native English.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪从法语借入 commence。它一直比本族语的 begin 更正式。

items.en: Commencement for the degree ceremony is a 19th-century American usage. The idea is that the ceremony begins the graduate's new life rather than closing their studies.
items.cn: 用 commencement 指学位授予典礼，是 19 世纪的美式用法。其理据是：典礼开启毕业生的新生活，而不是结束学业。

items.en: Modern usage keeps commence for ceremonies, contracts, works, and legal proceedings. Begin and start cover the ordinary, informal cases.
items.cn: 现代用法把 commence 留给典礼、合同、工程与法律程序；日常非正式场合则由 begin 和 start 承担。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the buying and selling of goods. It shares the comm- opening but comes from merx 'merchandise', not from 'begin'.
entries.definitionCN: 商业；贸易。同样以 comm- 开头，但来自 merx“商品”，与“开始”无关。

entries.definition: a remark or explanation. It shares the opening syllables but comes from a verb meaning 'to devise, think'.
entries.definitionCN: 评论；说明。开头音节相近，但来自意为“构思、思考”的动词。

entries.definition: to praise or recommend. It is close in sound but means handing something over with approval.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；推荐。读音接近，但意思是带着认可把某物交出去。

entries.definition: a beginning, or the graduation ceremony. It is the noun built directly on commence.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；毕业典礼。它是直接由 commence 构成的名词。

entries.definition: to start doing something. It is the ordinary native word, with no special formality.
entries.definitionCN: 开始。最普通的本族词，不带正式色彩。

entries.definition: to begin, often with a sense of setting something in motion. It is more physical and less ceremonial than commence.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；启动。更偏“让某物动起来”，不如 commence 正式。

entries.definition: to cause a process to begin. It stresses the first push rather than the ceremony of opening.
entries.definitionCN: 发起；启动。强调最初的一推，而不是开场仪式。

entries.definition: to start something publicly, especially a product or campaign. It adds publicity to the beginning.
entries.definitionCN: 正式推出；发起。在“开始”之外增加了公开宣传的意味。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin initium 'beginning', the French form of the verb, and the fixed phrases in which English still prefers commence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 initium“开端”、该动词的法语形式，以及英语仍偏好用 commence 的固定搭配。

normal.en: commence and initiate are cousins: both sit on Latin initium 'a beginning', which pictures a person stepping inside.
normal.cn: commence 与 initiate 是远亲：两者都建立在拉丁语 initium“开端”上，意象是“人迈步进入”。

normal.en: Commence is the formal twin of begin: meetings, ceremonies, contracts and court proceedings commence.
normal.cn: commence 是 begin 的正式孪生兄弟：会议、典礼、合同与法庭程序都用 commence。

normal.en: A lease commences on a date, because the contract crosses its threshold at that moment.
normal.cn: 租约在某日 commence，因为合同就在那一刻跨过自己的门槛。

normal.en: Commencement is the American graduation ceremony: it opens the next stage rather than closing the school years.
normal.cn: commencement 是美式毕业典礼：它开启下一阶段，而不是给学校岁月画句号。

normal.en: Commencing work means crossing from preparation into production, which is why factories and sites use the word.
normal.cn: commencing work 指从准备跨入生产，因此工厂与工地爱用这个词。

abstract.en: The core picture is a door: the activity already exists behind it, and commence is the act of stepping through.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一扇门：活动早就在门后存在，commence 是跨过去的那一步。

abstract.en: The word always looks forward: what is commencing is not the old state but the new one that has just been entered.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是朝前看：正在 commence 的不是旧状态，而是刚刚被进入的新状态。

abstract.en: Formality is the word's social dress: the same threshold is crossed by begin in speech and by commence in documents.
abstract.cn: 正式性是这个词的社会外衣：同一道门槛，口语用 begin 跨，文件用 commence 跨。

examples.en: Construction will commence as soon as the permit is issued.
examples.cn: 许可证一经签发，工程就会开工。

examples.en: The course commences with a short diagnostic test.
examples.cn: 这门课以一次简短的诊断测试开始。

examples.en: Her contract commences in September and runs for two years.
examples.cn: 她的合同九月生效，为期两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可门寺」——寺门一开，法会正式开始 → commence 开始

root: 源自拉丁语 initium“开端”、inire“走入、开始”，经俗拉丁语 *cominitiare 与古法语 comencier 进入英语，核心是“跨进门、正式起步”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of commence, all organised around a threshold. An activity, a ceremony, a contract, an era, a post, a degree ceremony, a lawsuit, and an opening chapter each have their own moment of stepping through.
sensesIntro.cn: commence 的八个义项都围绕一道门槛组织：一项活动、一场典礼、一份合同、一个时代、一个职位、一次毕业典礼、一场诉讼、开篇一章，各自都有跨过去的那一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door already open, and the step that carries someone across the threshold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇已经打开的门，以及把人带过门槛的那一步。

branches.en: THE FIRST STEP: an activity or a first chapter is what lies just inside the door.
branches.cn: 第一步：门内最近的东西，是一项活动或开篇一章。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC OPENING: ceremonies and graduations are entrances performed in front of others.
branches.cn: 公开开场：典礼与毕业式是在众人面前完成的“入场”。

branches.en: FORMAL FORCE: a contract or a lawsuit starts to bind only when its stated threshold is crossed.
branches.cn: 正式效力：合同或诉讼只有跨过既定门槛，才开始产生约束力。

branches.en: A PERIOD OPENS: an era commences without any person acting, because time itself is the thing that starts.
branches.cn: 时期开启：时代自行 commence，无需某个人动手，因为开始的是时间本身。

branches.en: A ROLE BEGINS: taking up a post is entering a chair that already exists.
branches.cn: 角色开始：上任就是进入一把早已存在的椅子。

intro.en: Commence carries the Latin beginning initium inside it. English adds -ment to make the noun and -ing to make the participle; the prefix com- here only intensifies.
intro.cn: commence 内部携带着拉丁语“开端”initium。英语加 -ment 构成名词，加 -ing 构成分词；这里的 com- 只起加强语气作用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around initium is large and still productive in English: initial, initiative, initiate, initiation, and the verb inire 'to go in'.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 initium 的拉丁词族很大，在英语里仍有生产力：initial、initiative、initiate、initiation，以及动词 inire“走入”。

definition_zh: v. 赞扬；推荐；托付
definition_en: to praise someone formally, or to recommend them
core_image: 经理在会议上当众表扬一名新员工
scene: 经理当众表扬了这位新员工，说她做事可靠。The manager commended the new employee for her reliability.

senses.title: To praise formally

senses.example: The judge commended the witness for her honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 法官称赞证人的诚实。
senses.why: Latin commendare joins com, fully, with mandare, to entrust.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 commendare 由 com（完全）与 mandare（托付）合成。

senses.title: To recommend or entrust
senses.definition: to hand something over to someone for safekeeping, or suggest it

senses.why: The older sense of entrusting survives in formal English.

definition_zh: 评论；意见；注释；评论（动词）
definition_en: a spoken or written remark about someone or something, a note explaining a text, or to make such a remark
core_image: 看完文章后在页边写下的一行小字
scene: 视频下面，网友留下一条简短的评价。He read the comment and smiled.
sceneCN: 这里 comment 指「评论；意见」（第 1 个义项：对事物的看法）；句意是他读了那条评论，笑了笑。

senses.title: A remark
senses.definition: something that you say or write to give your opinion
senses.definitionCN: 为表达看法而说或写的话
senses.example: He made a kind comment about her cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 他对她的厨艺说了句善意的评论。
senses.why: The everyday sense is a short remark offered to others.
senses.whyCN: 最日常的义项就是向别人说出的简短评语。

senses.title: A note explaining a text
senses.definition: a note added to a text to explain a difficult word or passage
senses.definitionCN: 加在文本旁解释难词或难句的注记
senses.example: The editor added a comment in the margin.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在页边加了一条注释。
senses.why: Scholars first wrote comments beside old books to explain them.
senses.whyCN: 学者最早在古书旁写注，用来解释原文。

senses.title: To remark
senses.definition: to say something that gives your opinion about a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 说出对某人或某事的看法
senses.example: Several readers commented on the article.
senses.exampleCN: 几位读者对这篇文章发表了评论。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to offer a comment.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把一条评论给出去。

intro.en: Comment comes from Latin commentum, a note or invention, built on comminisci, to devise.
intro.cn: comment 来自拉丁语 commentum（注记、构想），源自 comminisci（想出、构思）。

items.en: Comminisci meant to think up or devise something.
items.cn: comminisci 意为想出或构思出某物。

items.en: Commentum named a written note that explained a text.
items.cn: commentum 指解释文本的书面注记。

items.en: Old French coment kept the scholarly sense of a note.
items.cn: 古法语 coment 保留了注记的学术含义。

items.en: English comment first meant an explanatory note.
items.cn: 英语 comment 最初指解释性的注释。

items.en: It widened to any remark of opinion, spoken or posted online.
items.cn: 它的范围扩展到任何表达看法的话，无论口说还是网上发布。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape to comment, while the meaning group gives other words for a remark.

intro.en: Commerce comes from Latin commercium, a trading together, built on merx, merchandise.
intro.cn: commerce 来自拉丁语 commercium（互相交易），词根是 merx（货物）。

items.en: Merx meant goods for sale, the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: merx 意为待售的货物，是整族词的种子。

items.en: Commercium joined com-, together, with merx to mean exchange of goods.
items.cn: commercium 把表示一起的 com- 与 merx 结合，意为货物交换。

items.en: Old French commerce kept the sense of trade between places.
items.cn: 古法语 commerce 保留了各地之间贸易的含义。

items.en: English commerce named trade by sea and by land.
items.cn: 英语 commerce 指海上与陆上的贸易。

items.en: It now covers shops, banks, online sales and business life in general.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖商店、银行、网络销售以及一般的商务生活。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with signing away your own time, then move to wrong acts and to being handed into a prison.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从签下自己的时间开始，再走到错事与被送进监狱。

normal.en: Commit is to send yourself into something with no way back.
normal.cn: commit 就是把自己送进去，不留退路。

normal.en: The doubled t appears in committed and committing, but not in commit.
normal.cn: committed 与 committing 双写 t，但 commit 本身不双写。

normal.en: You commit a crime or an error, and you commit to a person or plan.
normal.cn: 你犯下罪行或错误，也把自己承诺给某个人或计划。

normal.en: Commit to memory means sending a fact into lasting storage.
normal.cn: 牢记就是把一个事实送进长期存储。

normal.en: A committed teacher gives more than the timetable asks.
normal.cn: 一位尽心尽力的老师，付出的比课表要求的多。

abstract.en: Picture a signature pressed hard enough to mark the page below.
abstract.cn: 想象签名用力到在下一页留下印痕。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door closing behind a person.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门在人身后关上。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burning at only one end, deliberately.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛被刻意只在一头燃烧。

examples.en: He committed himself to training every morning.
examples.cn: 他坚持每天早上训练。

examples.en: The clerk committed a small error in the list.
examples.cn: 职员在名单上犯了个小错。

examples.en: They committed the old files to memory.
examples.cn: 他们把旧档案牢牢记住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commit 记成 com（一起）加 mit（送出）：把自己整个送出去，就是承诺与投入。

root: 源自拉丁语 committere，com- 表示一起，mittere 表示送出，本义是交出去、托付，后引申为承诺投入与犯错。

sensesIntro.en: From handing yourself over to a task, to handing a wrong act to the record, and to handing a person into custody.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把自己交给一项任务，到把错事交给记录，再到把人交入监管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: staking your whole self on one thing with no way back.
core.cn: 核心意象：把自己整个人押在一件事上，不再回头。

branches.en: The promise sense is the everyday modern one.
branches.cn: 承诺义是现代最日常的义项。

branches.en: A crime is an act handed over to the record.
branches.cn: 罪行就是被交给记录的行为。

branches.en: Courts still use the old sense of handing a person over.
branches.cn: 法庭至今仍用「把人交出去」这个古老义项。

branches.en: Both a promise and a crime are acts you cannot easily undo.
branches.cn: 承诺与罪行都是不易撤回的行为。

branches.en: Devotion and custody both begin with a transfer of control.
branches.cn: 投入与收押都始于控制权的转移。

intro.en: Commit builds nouns with -ment and -al, and its past forms double the final t.
intro.cn: commit 用 -ment 与 -al 构成名词，过去式与分词双写词尾的 t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mittere, to send, also appears in mission, permit and submit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere（送出）也出现在 mission、permit 与 submit 之中。

items.meaning: promises, or does a wrong act
items.example: He commits one hour a day to reading.
items.exampleCN: 他每天拿出一小时读书。

items.meaning: gave full effort or carried out an act
items.example: They committed more money to the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们为这个计划投入了更多资金。

items.meaning: the act of promising or doing wrong
items.example: She is committing too much time to one task.
items.exampleCN: 她在一项任务上投入的时间太多。
这份工作需要真正的投入。

items.example: He has family commitments this weekend.
items.exampleCN: 他这周末有家里的事务。

items.meaning: the act of sending someone to prison or court
items.example: The committal hearing lasted an hour.
items.exampleCN: 交付审理的听证持续了一小时。

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.meaning: a task or authority entrusted to someone
items.example: The commission began its work in May.

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.example: The committee meets twice a month.

definition_zh: 承诺；投入；必须承担的事务
definition_en: a promise to do something, steady dedication to a cause, or a duty that you must carry out
core_image: 说出口就不再收回的那句保证
scene: 教练要求队员每天清晨到场训练。The team showed real commitment during the long season.
sceneCN: 这里 commitment 指「投入；奉献」（第 2 个义项：全心全意的付出）；句意是这支队伍在漫长的赛季里表现出真正的投入。

senses.title: A promise to do something
senses.definition: a firm promise that you will do something
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地答应去做某事的保证
senses.example: She made a commitment to call her parents weekly.
senses.exampleCN: 她承诺每周给父母打电话。
senses.why: The -ment ending turns the act of committing into the thing promised.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把承诺的动作变成被承诺下来的那件事。

senses.title: Dedication
senses.definition: steady effort and loyalty given to a person, job or cause
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某项工作或事业持续付出的努力与忠诚
senses.example: The team showed real commitment during the long season.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在漫长的赛季里表现出真正的投入。
senses.why: A promise kept day after day becomes visible dedication.
senses.whyCN: 一天天兑现的承诺，就变成了看得见的投入。

senses.title: A duty you must carry out
senses.definition: an obligation that takes your time and cannot be ignored
senses.definitionCN: 占用你的时间且无法回避的义务
senses.example: He has family commitments this weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 他这周末有家里的事务要处理。
senses.why: Each promise creates a duty, and the word names those duties in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 每个承诺都造出一份义务，这个词用复数来指这些义务。

intro.en: Commitment is commit plus -ment, the ending that turns an action into a thing.
intro.cn: commitment 由 commit 加 -ment 构成，词尾把动作变成事物。

items.en: Committere meant to entrust or hand over.
items.cn: committere 意为托付或交出。

items.en: Old French commettre supplied the verb commit.
items.cn: 古法语 commettre 提供了动词 commit。

items.en: English commit covered entrusting and carrying out acts.
items.cn: 英语 commit 兼指托付与实施行为。

items.en: Commitment appeared as the state of being pledged.
items.cn: commitment 出现，表示已被许诺约束的状态。

items.en: It widened to mean loyalty to work, people and causes.
items.cn: 它的含义扩展到对工作、他人与事业的忠诚。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns built on the commit stem, while the meaning group names promises and duties.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在 commit 词干上的名词，近义组列出承诺与义务。

entries.definition: the act of sending someone to prison or court
a group chosen to decide something
a person who travels to work regularly
great effort given to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目标付出的巨大努力

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a spoken promise, then move to daily dedication and to the duties that pile up around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一句说出口的承诺开始，再走到日复一日的投入与由此堆积的事务。

normal.en: Commit is the act, commitment is the thing you are now held to.
normal.cn: commit 是动作，commitment 是你此后必须遵守的那件事。

normal.en: A commitment kept for years looks exactly like dedication.
normal.cn: 坚持多年的承诺，看起来就是投入。

normal.en: Make a commitment, then honour it: two verbs, one promise.
normal.cn: 作出承诺，然后履行承诺：两个动作，一个诺言。

normal.en: Commitments in the plural often means a crowded calendar.
normal.cn: 复数形式的承诺，常常意味着排得满满的日程。

normal.en: The doubled t of commit stays in commitment.
normal.cn: commit 的双写 t 在 commitment 里保留下来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a quiet room to say yes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在安静的房间里举起的手，说出我愿意。

abstract.en: Picture a runner training on the same track in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者在雨中跑同一条跑道。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar filled with names and dates.
abstract.cn: 想象一本写满人名与日期的日历。

examples.en: She made a commitment to finish the course.
examples.cn: 她承诺要完成这门课程。

examples.en: The job demands real commitment from every member.
examples.cn: 这份工作要求每位成员真正投入。

examples.en: He has too many commitments to travel this month.
examples.cn: 他这个月事务太多，没法出行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commitment 记成 commit（承诺）加 ment（事情）：承诺下来的那件事，就是你要背起的责任。

root: 由 commit 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，词根上溯拉丁语 committere（托付），本义是被交托下来的事，后指承诺与投入。

sensesIntro.en: From a promise in words, to the effort that keeps it, and finally to the duties it creates.
sensesIntro.cn: 从口头说出的承诺，到维持它的付出，再到它带来的义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a promise spoken once and never taken back.
core.cn: 核心意象：说出口就不再收回的那句保证。

branches.en: The promise itself is the sense that names the word.
branches.cn: 承诺本身是这个词最直接的义项。

branches.en: Kept promises turn into visible dedication.
branches.cn: 被兑现的承诺会变成看得见的投入。

branches.en: In the plural the word means the duties filling your week.
branches.cn: 用复数时，这个词指填满你一周的那些事务。

branches.en: A promise and the effort behind it are one thing seen twice.
branches.cn: 承诺与它背后的付出，是同一件事的两次显现。

branches.en: Dedication to work and family duties often compete for the same hours.
branches.cn: 对工作的投入与家庭事务常常争夺同样的时间。

intro.en: Commitment is a -ment noun, and it keeps the doubled t of its verb.
intro.cn: commitment 是带 -ment 的名词，并保留了动词双写的 t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mittere, to send, links commitment with mission and submit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere（送出）把 commitment 与 mission、submit 连在一起。

items.example: Work commitments kept her in the city.
items.exampleCN: 工作上的事务让她留在了城里。

items.example: They commit two days a week to the club.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周为社团投入两天。
她是一位尽心尽力的老师。

items.meaning: the act of promising or giving effort
items.example: Committing to one plan is harder than making ten.
items.exampleCN: 投入一个计划比许下十个愿更难。

items.meaning: the act of sending someone to prison or court
items.example: The committal took place that morning.

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.meaning: authority or work entrusted to someone
items.example: The commission reported back in June.
items.exampleCN: 委员会六月提交了报告。

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.meaning: a group that carries out a task
refusing to state a clear position
items.exampleCN: 他给了一个不置可否的回答。

definition_zh: 委员会；专门小组
definition_en: a group of people chosen to make decisions or do a particular job for a larger organization
core_image: 长桌旁围坐一圈、举手投票的一群人
scene: 几个人围着长桌，为活动方案投票表决。The committee met on Monday to review the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 committee 指「委员会」（第 1 个义项：受选处理事务的团体）；句意是委员会周一开会审议这个方案。

senses.title: A group chosen to decide
senses.definition: a group of people appointed by a larger body to decide or manage something
senses.definitionCN: 由更大机构委派来决策或管理事务的一群人
senses.example: The committee approved the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会批准了新预算。
senses.why: A task is committed to a group, and the group takes the name of that trust.
senses.whyCN: 任务被托付给一群人，这群人便承接了这份托付的名字。

senses.title: A smaller working group
senses.definition: a small group formed inside an organization for one particular job
senses.definitionCN: 在组织内部为某项具体工作而设的小组
senses.example: A sports committee organized the summer games.
senses.exampleCN: 一个体育小组筹办了夏季运动会。
senses.why: Large bodies split tasks among small groups, and each is still a committee.
senses.whyCN: 大机构把任务分给小组，每个小组仍称作委员会。

intro.en: Committee is a Middle English noun from the verb commit, meaning a person to whom something is committed.
intro.cn: committee 是中古英语名词，出自动词 commit，本指被托付事务的人。

items.en: Committere meant to entrust something to someone.
items.cn: committere 意为把某事托付给某人。

items.en: Old French commettre and its noun forms carried the sense of trust.
items.cn: 古法语 commettre 及其名词形式都带有信任与托付之意。

items.en: A committe was first one person entrusted with a matter.
items.cn: 最初 committe 指受托办理某事的一个人。

items.en: The meaning shifted from one person to a whole body of people.
items.cn: 词义从一个人转移到一整群人的机构。

items.en: Committee now names any appointed decision-making group.
items.cn: 如今 committee 指任何受委派的决策团体。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns that echo the commit stem, while the meaning group names other decision-making bodies.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 commit 词干相呼应的名词，近义组列出其他决策机构。

entries.definition: the act of sending someone to prison or court
a person who travels to work regularly
a group that manages a company or body
a small group chosen to discuss or judge
entries.definitionCN: 专门讨论或评审的小组

entries.definition: an elected group that governs an area
entries.definitionCN: 管理一个地区的议事机构

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a circle of chairs, then move to the trust behind the title and to smaller working groups.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一圈椅子开始，再走到名称背后的托付与更小的工作组。

normal.en: Committee and commitment come from the same verb, one is people, one is promise.
normal.cn: committee 与 commitment 出自同一个动词，一个是人，一个是承诺。

normal.en: The word ends in -ee, but a committee does the work rather than receives it.
normal.cn: 词尾是 -ee，但委员会是做事的，而不是被做的。

normal.en: A committee meeting is where one decision needs many hands.
normal.cn: 委员会会议，就是一个决定需要许多双手的地方。

normal.en: Set up a committee whenever a job is too big for one desk.
normal.cn: 一项工作一张桌子办不完，就成立一个委员会。

normal.en: Two e and two t hide inside committee.
normal.cn: committee 里藏着两个 e 和两个 t。

abstract.en: Picture a long table with eight chairs and one lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，八把椅子，一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture hands rising slowly for a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象表决时一只只手缓缓举起。

abstract.en: Picture a folder passed from one member to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹在成员之间传递。

examples.en: The committee met on Monday to review the plan.
examples.cn: 委员会周一开会审议这个方案。

examples.en: She joined the school safety committee.
examples.cn: 她加入了学校的安全委员会。

examples.en: The committees will report back next month.
examples.cn: 各委员会下个月提交报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 committee 记成 commit（托付）加 tee：被托付一群人办事，这群人就是委员会。

root: 由动词 commit 派生而来，词根为拉丁语 committere（托付），本义是被托付事务的人，后转指受委派的团体。

sensesIntro.en: From one trusted person, to the body that decides, and finally to any small group given a single job.
sensesIntro.cn: 从受信任的一个人，到作出决定的机构，再到承担单项任务的小组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people around a long table, raising hands to decide.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌旁围坐一圈、举手投票的一群人。

branches.en: The decision-making body is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 决策机构是今天的主要义项。

branches.en: A small group inside an organization is the same idea at smaller scale.
branches.cn: 组织内部的小组，是同一想法在更小尺度上的体现。

branches.en: Both a national body and a school group work by meeting.
branches.cn: 全国性机构与校内小组都靠开会运作。

branches.en: Size changes, but the trust placed in the group does not.
branches.cn: 规模会变，但托付给这群人的信任不变。

branches.en: The smallest committee is often the one that gets things done.
branches.cn: 最小的委员会往往才是真正把事办成的那个。

intro.en: Committee is a noun from commit, and it keeps the doubled t in the singular and plural.
intro.cn: committee 是由 commit 派生的名词，单复数都保留双写的 t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mittere, to send, sits under the whole commit family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere（送出）支撑着整个 commit 家族。

items.example: Three committees share the same room.
items.exampleCN: 三个委员会共用同一间房。

items.example: They commit the matter to a small group.
items.exampleCN: 他们把这件事交给一个小组。
成员们以真正的投入服务。

items.example: The committee is a committed group.
items.exampleCN: 这个委员会是一群尽心尽力的人。

items.example: The committal was delayed by a week.

items.structure: related noun from the same root

items.exampleCN: 这个委员会与那个委员会一同开会。

items.meaning: a smaller committee inside a larger one
items.exampleCN: 一个小组委员会起草了规则。

items.meaning: a male member of a committee

definition_zh: n. 商品；有用的东西
definition_en: a raw material or product that can be bought and sold
core_image: 成袋的咖啡豆堆在交易所大厅里
scene: 咖啡豆在全球市场上是一种重要商品。Coffee beans are a major commodity on world markets.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commodity 指商品；句意是咖啡豆在全球市场上是一种重要商品。

senses.title: A tradable product
senses.definition: a raw material or basic product traded in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 大宗交易的原料或基本产品
senses.example: Oil is the world's most traded commodity.
senses.exampleCN: 石油是世界上交易量最大的商品。
senses.why: Latin commoditas meant convenience, then advantage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 commoditas 意为便利，后指好处。

senses.title: Anything useful and valued
senses.definition: something valuable that people want or need
senses.definitionCN: 人们想要或需要的宝贵之物
senses.example: Clean water is a precious commodity here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里干净的水是珍贵之物。
senses.why: The figurative sense treats value as merchandise.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义把「价值」当作货物。

intro.en: Commodity began as a word for convenience and advantage.
intro.cn: commodity 最初指便利与好处。

items.en: Commodus means convenient or suitable.
items.cn: commodus 意为便利、合适。

items.en: Commoditas means convenience, then advantage.
items.cn: commoditas 意为便利，后指好处。

items.en: Commodity meant a benefit or profit.
items.cn: 十五世纪 commodity 意为益处或利润。

items.en: It came to mean goods for sale.
items.cn: 十八世纪它指待售货物。

items.en: Commodity now names raw materials.
items.cn: 现代 commodity 指原材料。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the commod- shape; the near-meaning group names things sold.
note.cn: 形近组共享 commod- 词形；近义组列出可售之物。

normalIntro.en: A commodity is something useful enough to be sold.
normalIntro.cn: commodity 就是有用到可以出售的东西。

normal.en: Commodus means convenient.
normal.cn: commodus 意为便利。

normal.en: Commoditas meant advantage.
normal.cn: commoditas 意为好处。

normal.en: Then it meant a profit.
normal.cn: 后来它指利润。

normal.en: Today a commodity is traded.
normal.cn: 如今 commodity 是可交易的商品。

normal.en: Even time can be a commodity.
normal.cn: 连时间也可以是「商品」。

abstract.en: Sacks of beans on a trading floor.
abstract.cn: 交易所大厅里的一袋袋豆子。

abstract.en: A price moving all day.
abstract.cn: 整天波动的价格。

abstract.en: Water sold by the bottle.
abstract.cn: 按瓶出售的水。

examples.en: Wheat is a commodity traded worldwide.
examples.cn: 小麦是全球交易的商品。

examples.en: Good teachers are a rare commodity.
examples.cn: 好老师是稀缺资源。

examples.en: Commodity prices rose sharply last year.
examples.cn: 去年商品价格大幅上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: com（共同）+ modus（尺度）→ commodus（合适）→ 合用的东西，即商品。

root: 拉丁 commodus（合适的）→ commoditas（便利、好处）→ 英语 commodity

sensesIntro.en: What is convenient becomes what is profitable, and then what is sold.
sensesIntro.cn: 「便利」变成「有利」，再变成「可出售」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sacks of beans stacked on a trading floor
core.cn: 核心意象：交易所里堆叠的豆袋

branches.en: Oil sold by the barrel.
branches.cn: 按桶出售的石油。

branches.en: Grain priced each morning.
branches.cn: 每天早晨定价的谷物。

branches.en: Clean water in a dry town.
branches.cn: 缺水小镇的干净水。

branches.en: Trust treated as something valued.
branches.cn: 被视作有价值之物的信任。

branches.en: A useful thing with a price on it.
branches.cn: 标着价格的有用之物。

intro.en: Commodity is built from fitting and measuring pieces; the list adds trade words.
intro.cn: commodity 由「合适」与「尺度」词素构成；下面列出贸易词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin commodus is fitting, commoditas is advantage, and mercari is to trade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 commodus 意为合适，commoditas 意为好处，mercari 意为贸易。

latinEntries.exampleCN: commoditas 产生 commodity。
commodus 产生 commodious 与 commodity。
mercari 产生 merchant 与 market。

definition_zh: 常见的；共同的；普通的
definition_en: happening often, shared by many people, or ordinary and not special
core_image: 街角人人都走的那条普通小路
scene: 这种鸟在城里随处可见，几乎每个公园都有。Rain is common here in early summer.
sceneCN: 这里 common 指「常见的」（第 1 个义项：经常出现）；句意是初夏时节这里常下雨。

senses.title: Happening often
senses.definition: existing or happening very often in a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 在某地或某群体中经常出现或发生
senses.example: Heavy rain is common in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区常下大雨。
senses.why: The Latin root meant shared, and what many share is what happens often.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为共有，而多数人共有的东西就是经常出现的东西。

senses.title: Shared by many
senses.definition: belonging to or used by two or more people together
senses.definitionCN: 由两人或更多人共同拥有或使用的
senses.example: The two neighbours share a common wall.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家邻居共用一堵墙。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: communis meant belonging to all.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：communis 意为属于所有人。

senses.title: Ordinary, not special
senses.definition: plain and usual, without any special quality
senses.definitionCN: 平常的，没有特别之处的
senses.example: It was just a common chair, nothing rare.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是一把普通的椅子，没什么稀奇。
senses.why: What belongs to everyone is also nothing special, so shared becomes plain.
senses.whyCN: 属于所有人的东西也就不稀奇，于是共有变成了普通。

intro.en: Common comes from Latin communis, shared by all, through Old French comun.
intro.cn: common 经古法语 comun 上溯拉丁语 communis，意为众人共有。

items.en: Communis meant shared or belonging to all.
items.cn: communis 意为共有的或属于所有人的。

items.en: Communitas named the community that holds things in common.
items.cn: communitas 指共有事物的共同体。

items.en: Old French comun described what many people share.
items.cn: 古法语 comun 描述许多人共有的东西。

items.en: English common covered shared land and shared customs.
items.cn: 英语 common 既指共有的土地，也指共同的习俗。

items.en: It widened to mean frequent and also plain.
items.cn: 它的含义扩展到频繁出现以及平常普通。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in spelling to common, while the meaning group names what is usual.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 common 拼写相近的词，近义组列出表示平常与普遍的词。

entries.definition: a small community sharing work and goods
entries.definitionCN: 共同生活与劳作的社群

entries.definition: found over a large area or among many people

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a path everyone walks, then move to things held together and to plain everyday objects.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从人人都会走的小路开始，再走到共有的东西与平常的物件。

normal.en: Communis means shared, so common things belong to everyone, including habits.
normal.cn: communis 意为共有，所以 common 的东西属于所有人，习惯也一样。

normal.en: In common is the phrase for what two people share.
normal.cn: in common 就是用来表示两人共有什么的说法。

normal.en: Common sense is judgement shared by most people.
normal.cn: 常识就是多数人共有的判断力。

normal.en: The comparative is commoner, not more common, in careful writing.
normal.cn: 在讲究的写作里，比较级用 commoner，而不用 more common。

normal.en: Add un- and rare appears: uncommon.
normal.cn: 加上 un-，罕见的意思就出现了：uncommon。

abstract.en: Picture a worn path across a corner of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象草地一角被踩出的小径。

abstract.en: Picture two flats sharing one thin wall.
abstract.cn: 想象两套公寓共用一堵薄墙。

abstract.en: Picture a plain wooden chair in a plain room.
abstract.cn: 想象一间素净房间里的一把素木椅。

examples.en: Rain is common here in early summer.
examples.cn: 初夏时节这里常下雨。

examples.en: The two friends have a lot in common.
examples.cn: 这两个朋友有很多共同之处。

examples.en: It was only a common mistake, easily fixed.
examples.cn: 这不过是个常见的错误，很容易改。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 common 记成 com（一起）加 mon：大家一起都有的，就是共有的、常见的、普通的。

root: 源自拉丁语 communis（共有），经古法语 comun 进入英语，本义是众人共享，后引申为常见与普通。

sensesIntro.en: From what everyone shares, to what happens often, and finally to what is simply plain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从众人共有，到经常发生，再到平平常常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a well-worn path at a street corner that everyone uses.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角人人都走的那条普通小路。

branches.en: Frequent occurrence is the sense most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 经常发生是学习者最先接触到的义项。

branches.en: Shared ownership is the oldest sense and still very alive.
branches.cn: 共有是最古老的义项，至今仍然活跃。

branches.en: What is shared by all loses any mark of specialness.
branches.cn: 众人共有之物，也就失去了特别之处。

branches.en: A common habit is a habit many people share.
branches.cn: 常见的习惯就是许多人共有的习惯。

branches.en: Common land and a common chair both belong to no one in particular.
branches.cn: 公共土地与普通椅子都不专属于某个人。

intro.en: Common is an adjective base that grows with -ly, -ness, un- and compound forms.
intro.cn: common 是形容词词基，靠 -ly、-ness、un- 与复合形式扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin communis, shared, also gives community and communicate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis（共有）也给出了 community 与 communicate。

items.meaning: more common, or a person without a title
items.example: This bird is commoner in the south.
It is the commonest mistake in the book.
items.exampleCN: 这是书里最常见的错误。

items.example: The plant is commonly found near water.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物常在水边见到。

items.example: Snow is uncommon in this city.
The commonness of the name surprised him.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字的普遍程度让他吃惊。

items.meaning: so usual that it attracts no notice
items.exampleCN: 视频通话如今已司空见惯。

items.meaning: good judgement shared by most people
items.example: Use common sense before you decide.
The talks found common ground at last.
items.exampleCN: 会谈终于找到了共同点。

definition_zh: adj. 平常的 n. 老生常谈；平常事
definition_en: ordinary and not interesting; also an everyday remark
core_image: 街头人人都在扫码付款，没人再抬头看
scene: 手机支付如今已很平常，不再让人惊讶。Paying by phone is now commonplace and surprises no one.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commonplace 指平常的；句意是手机支付如今已很平常，不再让人惊讶。

senses.title: Ordinary and unremarkable
senses.definition: so usual that it no longer attracts attention
senses.definitionCN: 平常到不再引人注意
senses.example: Electric cars are becoming commonplace.
senses.exampleCN: 电动车正变得司空见惯。
senses.why: English calqued Latin locus communis, a common place.
senses.whyCN: 英语仿译拉丁语 locus communis（共同之处）。

senses.title: A trite remark
senses.definition: a remark that is true but dull because it is repeated
senses.definitionCN: 因反复而显得乏味的正确说法
senses.example: His speech was full of commonplaces.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演讲满是老生常谈。
senses.why: The noun sense came from rhetorical handbooks.
senses.whyCN: 名词义来自修辞手册。

intro.en: Commonplace translates a Latin phrase meaning a shared place.
intro.cn: commonplace 直译拉丁语中「共同的处所」这一短语。

items.en: Locus means a place.
items.cn: locus 意为地方。

items.en: Communis means shared.
items.cn: communis 意为共同的。

items.en: The phrase names a general topic.
items.cn: 这一短语指一般性话题。

items.en: English coined commonplace from the phrase.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语由该短语造出 commonplace。

items.en: It came to mean dull and trite.
items.cn: 十九世纪它获得「平庸陈腐」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the common- opening; the near-meaning group names the ordinary.
note.cn: 形近组共享 common- 开头；近义组列出普通之物。

normalIntro.en: A commonplace is literally a common place, so common it is dull.
normalIntro.cn: commonplace 字面就是「共同之处」，共同到显得乏味。

normal.en: Locus means place.
normal.cn: locus 意为地方。

normal.en: Communis means shared.
normal.cn: communis 意为共同的。

normal.en: A common place is a shared topic.
normal.cn: common place 是共同话题。

normal.en: So commonplace means ordinary.
normal.cn: 因此 commonplace 意为平常。

normal.en: A dull saying is a commonplace.
normal.cn: 乏味的说法就是老生常谈。

abstract.en: A street everyone walks past.
abstract.cn: 人人走过却不看的街。

abstract.en: A phrase worn smooth.
abstract.cn: 被磨得光滑的一句话。

abstract.en: Rain on a Tuesday.
abstract.cn: 周二的雨。

examples.en: Smartphones are now commonplace in schools.
examples.cn: 智能手机在学校已很常见。

examples.en: The essay repeats one commonplace after another.
examples.cn: 这篇文章堆满老生常谈。

examples.en: Such accidents are sadly commonplace.
examples.cn: 这类事故不幸地很常见。

dict_mnemonic.text: common（共同）+ place（地方）→ 人人共有的地方，即平常事、老生常谈。

root: 拉丁 locus communis（共同之处）→ 英语 common + place → commonplace

sensesIntro.en: Common enough to be dull, whether an event or a phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: 平常到乏味，不论是事件还是说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street scene no one bothers to look at
core.cn: 核心意象：没人愿意多看一眼的街景

branches.en: A phone paying for coffee.
branches.cn: 用手机买咖啡。

branches.en: An event nobody reports.
branches.cn: 无人报道的事件。

branches.en: A speech of worn phrases.
branches.cn: 满是旧话的演讲。

branches.en: A saying everyone knows.
branches.cn: 人人都知道的说法。

branches.en: The usual, as event or as remark.
branches.cn: 平常之物，无论事件或说法。

intro.en: Commonplace joins two plain English words; the list adds everyday pieces.
intro.cn: commonplace 由两个普通英语词合成；下面列出日常词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin communis is shared, locus is a place, and ordo is order.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis 意为共同的，locus 意为地方，ordo 意为次序。

latinEntries.exampleCN: locus communis 变成英语 commonplace。
communis 产生 common 与 community。
ordo 产生 order 与 ordinary。

definition_zh: n. （政治）共同体，联邦；英联邦
definition_en: a group of states with shared interests, or a state governed for the common good
core_image: 多国旗帜并排挂在同一面墙前
scene: 这些国家组成一个共享语言与法律的联邦。These states form a commonwealth bound by shared law.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commonwealth 指共同体；句意是这些国家组成一个共享语言与法律的联邦。

senses.title: A political community
senses.definition: a group of states or people united by shared interests
senses.definitionCN: 因共同利益联合的国家或人群
senses.example: The islands formed a loose commonwealth.
senses.exampleCN: 这些岛屿组成松散的联邦。
senses.why: English translated Latin res publica, the public thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语直译拉丁语 res publica（公共之物）。

senses.title: The Commonwealth of Nations
senses.definition: the association of Britain and many former colonies
senses.definitionCN: 英国与许多前殖民地的联合体
senses.example: She represented the country at the Commonwealth summit.
senses.exampleCN: 她代表国家出席英联邦峰会。
senses.why: The name was adopted in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 这一名称在二十世纪被采用。

intro.en: Commonwealth is an English translation of the Latin phrase for public affairs.
intro.cn: commonwealth 是拉丁语「公共事务」短语的英语直译。

items.en: Res means a thing or affair.
items.cn: res 意为事物或事务。

items.en: Res publica means public affairs.
items.cn: res publica 意为公共事务。

items.en: Commonwealth translated that phrase.
items.cn: 十五世纪 commonwealth 直译该短语。

items.en: Cromwell named his state a commonwealth.
items.cn: 十七世纪克伦威尔以 commonwealth 称呼其政权。

items.en: The modern association took the name.
items.cn: 二十世纪现代联合体采用了这一名称。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the common- opening; the near-meaning group names unions of states.
note.cn: 形近组共享 common- 开头；近义组列出国家联合体。

entries.definition: A state with an elected head.

normalIntro.en: A commonwealth is shared wealth, shared in government.
normalIntro.cn: commonwealth 是共同的财富，在治理上共享。

normal.en: Common means shared.
normal.cn: common 意为共同的。

normal.en: Wealth means well-being.
normal.cn: wealth 意为福祉。

normal.en: Commonwealth is shared well-being.
normal.cn: commonwealth 是共享的福祉。

normal.en: Res publica is its Latin model.
normal.cn: res publica 是其拉丁语原型。

normal.en: The Commonwealth links former colonies.
normal.cn: 英联邦联结前殖民地。

abstract.en: Flags lined along one wall.
abstract.cn: 并排挂在墙上的旗帜。

abstract.en: A table with many chairs.
abstract.cn: 摆着许多椅子的桌子。

abstract.en: A law read in many accents.
abstract.cn: 用许多口音读出的同一条法律。

examples.en: The region became a commonwealth in 1975.
examples.cn: 该地区于 1975 年成为共同体。

examples.en: She spoke at the Commonwealth meeting.
examples.cn: 她在英联邦会议上发言。

examples.en: The two nations share a commonwealth of law.
examples.cn: 两国共享一套法律传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: common（共同）+ wealth（福祉）→ 共同福祉的政体，即共同体、联邦。

root: 拉丁 res publica（公共事务）→ 英语 common（共同）+ wealth（福祉）→ commonwealth

sensesIntro.en: A state for the common good, and the modern club of former colonies.
sensesIntro.cn: 为共同福祉的政体，以及现代前殖民地联合体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many flags hanging side by side on one wall
core.cn: 核心意象：一面墙上并排挂着许多旗帜

branches.en: Islands joined in one polity.
branches.cn: 联合为一个政体的岛屿。

branches.en: A state run for public good.
branches.cn: 为公共利益治理的国家。

branches.en: A summit of former colonies.
branches.cn: 前殖民地峰会。

branches.en: Games held under its name.
branches.cn: 以其名举办的运动会。

branches.en: Shared rule, ancient or modern.
branches.cn: 共享的治理，或古或今。

intro.en: Commonwealth joins shared and well-being; the list adds state pieces.
intro.cn: commonwealth 由「共同」与「福祉」合成；下面列出政体词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin res is a thing, publica is public, and foedus is a treaty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res 意为事物，publica 意为公共的，foedus 意为条约。

latinEntries.exampleCN: res publica 变成英语 commonwealth。
communis 产生 common 与 community。
foedus 产生 federal 与 federation。
